root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting or splitting something, with related developments toward shaping, opening, producing something remarkable, and fabricating speech or claims.
root_idea.development: The lexical development contrasts cutting to repair or properly shape with cutting that damages or opens; figurative branches include bursting open, excelling, becoming confounded, and fabricating falsehood. The Quranic fabrication sense is especially associated with اِفْتَرَى and its derivatives.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Plural passive-participial occurrence presented under the singular citation form.
Plural active-participial occurrences presented under the singular citation form.

senses.definition: To fabricate or invent a falsehood.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is an imperfect form used for inventing a claim or allegation; the supplied QAC metadata labels this group Form I.

senses.definition: To fabricate, forge, or invent falsehood.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for fabricating lies or claims, including falsely attributing statements, partners, or other matters to God. It may occur with عَلَيْهِ, ‘against him,’ and includes both active and passive constructions in the Quran.

senses.definition: Remarkable, extraordinary, or of great magnitude.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا, the term describes something astonishing or extraordinary; the explanations ‘great,’ ‘wonderful,’ and ‘fabricated’ are treated as related interpretations of one underlying sense.

senses.definition: One who fabricates or invents falsehood.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle used substantively for a person who makes up lies or false claims; the Quran uses both singular and plural forms.
A passive participle describing something presented as fabricated or not genuine; the Quran supplies singular and plural forms.

senses.definition: Fabrication or invention of falsehood; false attribution.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for the act of fabricating claims, especially false claims made against God or attributed to Him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit or cut something lengthwise, especially leather or skin; the cutting may be described as either proper or faulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of cutting a hide, garment, receptacle, wound, or similar object. The lexical contrast between cutting well and cutting badly is preserved without making either result universal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To measure, cut, work, sew, or manufacture an object so as to make it sound and properly formed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of leather goods such as sandals, a hide, or a leathern water-bag.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter or butcher with vehemence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic use expressing excess or force in killing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attack someone with censure or satire; to blame or reproach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to speech directed against a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To traverse or cross a land or country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension in which travelling across land is conceived as cutting across it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To accomplish an extraordinary deed or excel in an undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Idiomatic usage can also describe someone as excelling in work or magnifying his words about a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of lightning, to shine or glisten with flickering light and continue in the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage applied to lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confounded, perplexed, astonished, or unable to determine the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person overcome by fright, bewilderment, or astonishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become slit, rent, or cleft; figuratively, to burst open or become distinct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of skin or a garment becoming torn, earth bursting forth with springs, and night becoming distinct from dawn. Figurative descriptions may emphasize disclosure, emergence, multitude, or wide extent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clamour or confused mixture of cries, shouts, or noises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for a tumultuous combination of sounds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lie or falsehood; also a defamatory allegation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun derived in relation to fabrication and used for false or defamatory speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair or case of great magnitude, gravity, or importance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal extension describing the seriousness or moment of a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slit or cut lengthwise, especially of a skin or hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a hide or similar material that has been cut open.
The form is explained as connected with something slit or opened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A forger or fabricator of lies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of a person, distinct in headword from the Quranic active participle مُفْتَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk at the time when it is milked.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the repeated idiom الفَرِيَّ الفَرِيَّ as an imperative-like expression.
A fixed expression in which الفِرَى is the plural of فِرْيَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leathern water-bag made in a sound or proper manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal designation for a well-made water-bag.
